parental leave = unpaid or paid time off to care for a child, available to eligible parents
unpaid leave = time away from work that is agreed but not paid
annual leave = paid holiday entitlement for a year of work
workplace pension = a retirement savings scheme arranged through the employer
fringe benefits = extras besides wages, such as meals, insurance or a travel card
perks of the job = informal extras that come with a particular role
performance-related pay = pay that rises or falls with measured results
sales commission = pay calculated as a percentage of sales or deals
take-home pay = what you actually receive after tax and other deductions
pay rise = an increase in wages or salary
pay freeze = a period when wages are not increased
gender pay gap = the difference between average pay of men and women in an organisation or economy
equal pay = the principle that people doing the same work should receive the same pay
time off in lieu = free time given instead of extra pay for additional hours worked
workload = the amount of work a person or team is expected to complete
anti-social hours = working times that clash with evenings, nights or weekends
on call = available to work if needed, often outside normal hours
occupational stress = harmful pressure caused by the demands of a job
repetitive strain injury = pain or damage from repeating the same movement at work
health and safety = rules and practices that protect people from harm at work
